rubric_source: No rubric file present in the worksheet folder; standard one-key, difficulty 2–3, all-six within-item distinctness, and all-190 cross-item method/response-format review used.

criteria.one_key: Exactly one offered choice is correct under standard written American English or exact stated mathematics.
criteria.difficulty: 1 easy, 2 moderate, 3 challenging, 4 advanced; target is 2 or 3.
criteria.within_item_distinctness: Every unordered pair of the four choices must have distinct requested form pairs or unequal exact numerical values; all six pairs per item are explicitly recorded.

cross_item_repetition_scale.1: Same broad domain only; decisive method or response form differs.
cross_item_repetition_scale.2: Same response family or a substantial operation, but a different decisive rule, operation, or response goal.
cross_item_repetition_scale.3: Strong repetition: same response family and same dominant solution procedure; a student can carry the same sequence of steps to both with only surface words, expression details, or numbers changed.

criteria.weak_distractor: A wrong choice with no plausible single-step misconception or a much less diagnostic path than peer distractors.

item_reviews.key_basis: Relative-clause who takes plural clerks; one of the clerks is singular.

There are ten integers 4 through 13; only roots 5 and 12 fail the nonzero test.
The gerund phrase Preparing the meals is singular; cooks is plural.
With neither/nor and either/or, the nearer subjects assistants and curator control the two verbs.
The number takes singular is; a number of readers takes plural are.
The condition reduces to x≤8, giving 4,5,6,7,8: five integers.
Most of the letters is plural; most of the mail is singular mass-noun agreement.
Each of the clerks takes keeps; Ava and Ben each takes plural review.
Inverted subjects returns and book are plural and singular respectively.
x(x+5)≤36 holds for positive domain x≤4; the maximum is 4.
